parts.value: Let $I=[0,2]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,i]\times \{-i\}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$

Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}=\{x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I\}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=1,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{1}=[0,1]\times \{-1\}=\{(k,-1)\,:\,k\in [0,1]\}.
$$

This represents a horizontal line segment from the point $(0,-1)$ to the point $(1,-1)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/a39443fd1b3764ff60c0c052085134ad7eeda6759c07c4d936fc03cd121f72dd.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,i]\times \{-i\}=\{(k,-i)\,:\,k\in [0,i]\}
$$

is the horizontal line segment from the point $(0,-i)$ to the point $(i,-i).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/7f18af14c55acc4bc2cd63b601dba0bde3cd51c0284b398b401c854537003926.png)

There are no points that lie in all sets. Therefore, the intersection of the indexed sets is $∅,$ the empty set.
